messages.content: Write a contemporary American fiction scene about two longtime adult friends walking home after work. Let their conversation wander naturally between whatever comes to mind. They can move from something that happened today to an old memory, then to weekend plans, then to something completely trivial. Do not force the conversation to stay on one subject. Output only story prose.

The grocery bag in Jordan’s hand was cutting into her fingers by the time they reached the corner.

“You bought too much.”

Alex glanced at the bag. “I bought three things.”

“You bought three heavy things.”

“That’s different.”

“Not when I’m the one carrying the sparkling water.”

Jordan took the bag back before Alex could grab it. “I’m fine.”

“You always say that right before you drop something.”

“I have never dropped anything.”

Alex looked at her.

Jordan thought about it. “Okay. Once.”

“Twice.”

“The yogurt was slippery.”

“Yogurt is not known for being athletic.”

She laughed and swung the bag lightly at her side. “Remember when you tried to make that cheesecake?”

“I remember you eating half of it.”

“I was supporting you.”

“You were supporting the cheesecake.”

“Same thing.”

They crossed the street, then walked another block before Jordan said, “I checked the cabins again.”

“For the lake trip?”

“Yeah. There’s one with a porch.”

“You hate porches.”

“I hate that one porch.”

“The haunted-looking one?”

“It wasn't haunted.”

“You wouldn't go outside after dark.”

“It had raccoons.”

“You saw one raccoon.”

“I saw its eyes.”

Alex laughed. “That raccoon owned you.”

“Anyway, I’m taking the porch cabin.”

“Sure you are.”

They kept walking, still arguing about the raccoon, until Jordan noticed they had already passed the turn they were supposed to take.
